queue.topic: Executing and using a power of attorney from abroad for Indian property and court matters: who can be the attorney, general versus special power, execution before a notary or Indian consular officer, apostille under the Hague Convention versus consular attestation (and which countries), stamping within three months of receipt in India under the Indian Stamp Act and State variations, registration under the Registration Act 1908 (sections 32, 33, 18 and 19 as applicable), use for sale, mortgage, litigation (Order III CPC, who may appear), revocation, death of principal, the power of attorney is not a title document (Suraj Lamp and Industries v State of Haryana, 2012) and what that means for sale deeds, and recognised pitfalls. Cover the practical order of steps with the documents at each step and the points that remain unsettled by State. The four Labour Codes in operation: what changed for employers and workers on wages, standing orders, fixed-term employment, retrenchment and closure thresholds, social security, inspector-cum-facilitator and compliance, and the open questions (status of State rules).

Infrastructure and PPP disputes: termination payments, force majeure and change in law, writ jurisdiction versus arbitration in public contracts, and what recent Supreme Court and High Court rulings mean for concessionaires and authorities.

Power sector disputes: change in law claims, deemed distribution licensee, true-up and carrying cost, regulatory jurisdiction, APTEL's recent line of decisions, and allocation of risk in power purchase agreements.

Food safety enforcement in India: FSSAI labelling and claims (front-of-pack, '100%' and similar claims), licence suspension and cancellation, improvement notices, recall, adjudication and appeals, and what the courts have said recently about proportionality and process.

GST litigation after the GST Appellate Tribunal: where an assessee now stands on show cause notices, pre-deposit, input tax credit denial, writ jurisdiction, limitation under the applicable sections, and appeals; state only what you confirm.

Consumer protection and e-commerce: CCPA enforcement, dark patterns, misleading advertisements, product liability, platform liability, and the interplay with RERA, banking and insurance disputes at consumer fora.

Debt recovery today: SARFAESI, DRT, the Commercial Courts route, and IBC Section 7 and 9 compared; guarantor and promoter exposure; limitation and the common procedural traps; and what recent Supreme Court rulings changed.
Shareholder disputes in India: oppression and mismanagement before the NCLT, who can file, interim relief, buy-out and winding-up remedies, and what recent NCLAT and Supreme Court rulings say.
Redevelopment and joint development agreements: society and developer disputes, delay and termination remedies, RERA, and the arbitration and civil court routes.
Trade mark enforcement in India: infringement and passing off, well-known marks, interim injunctions, and what recent High Court rulings say on evidence and delay.
Enforcing foreign awards in India, and interim relief in foreign-seated arbitrations: Part II of the Arbitration Act, grounds of refusal, limitation and recent rulings.
Joint ventures and acquisitions in India: key contractual protections and regulatory approvals (CCI, FEMA, SEBI), and common drafting traps.

Commercial disputes in Noida and Greater Noida (Gautam Buddh Nagar): which court has jurisdiction, how the Commercial Courts Act 2015 works there in practice (pre-institution mediation under Section 12A, case management, summary judgment, timelines), and how appeals and writs reach the Allahabad High Court. Verify the court structure, the territorial jurisdiction rules and the current position from official and reported sources; write for businesses and practitioners based in Noida.

Arbitration for Noida and Delhi NCR businesses: seat versus venue, which High Court exercises supervisory jurisdiction (Delhi or Allahabad) for Sections 9, 11, 34 and 37, institutional arbitration options in the region, interim relief and enforcement of awards against assets in Uttar Pradesh. Verify every jurisdiction point and case citation from sources.

Real estate disputes in Noida and Greater Noida: the roles of the Noida and Greater Noida development authorities, UP RERA and the UP Real Estate Appellate Tribunal, allottee remedies for delayed possession, lease and allotment cancellations, and the Supreme Court and Allahabad High Court decisions that govern them. Verify the institutions, limitation and procedure from official and reported sources.

Recovery and insolvency for lenders and borrowers in Noida: SARFAESI action, the Debts Recovery Tribunal and Appellate Tribunal with jurisdiction over Uttar Pradesh, Section 138 Negotiable Instruments Act complaints at Noida courts, and which NCLT bench hears IBC petitions against companies registered in Uttar Pradesh. Verify bench and territorial jurisdiction from official notifications and reported decisions.
